free_tier.stated: Quoted: '$2M in prizes. 3 tracks. Open source progress toward AGI.' The ARC-AGI-3 track is '$850K Total' with a '$700K' grand prize, a '$75K (guaranteed)' top-score award split 40/15/10/5/5 thousand, and two '$75K (guaranteed)' milestone rounds at June 30 and September 30, 2026. The Paper Prize pays '$75K (guaranteed)' to the highest-scoring paper and '$50K / $20K / $5K' for first to third. Entry is a Kaggle competition, and payment is conditional, quoted: 'All leading participants are expected to open source their solutions to be eligible for a prize.'

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The competition supplies the compute: entry is a Kaggle notebook, and the corpus already holds Kaggle's weekly 30 hour GPU quota and free TPU in compute/kaggle-notebooks, so the prize can be contested with no card. A guaranteed milestone award then buys GPU at spot rates. What breaks the chain is the open-source condition: the solution must be public to be paid, so the same work cannot be sold twice.

limits.value: an open-source release of the whole solution is a condition of payment and the modal outcome is zero: entry is free and open, but the money is decided on a leaderboard whose top places are contested by funded labs, while the $700K grand prize is written as a forward offer ('Awarded to the first eligible agent that scores 100%') rather than as an accumulated balance.

notes: The distinction that matters here is that the entry cost is zero and the tool is a browser notebook, so the downside is time only. Two framings were tested: an AI-lab marketing exercise with no realistic solo winner, and a funded research budget with a handful of large awards. The milestone structure supports the second for a solo entrant: two guaranteed rounds of USD 75,000 across three places each, decided on a leaderboard rather than on a grant application. The page states the grand prize as a forward-looking offer ('the first eligible agent'), not as a fact about past results, and this record adds no claim about whether it has been won.
